{"markdown": "## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of RAG1 p.Arg404Gln (UniProt P15918), and which single computational test checks it? [E1]

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies RAG1 p.Arg404Gln as Pathogenic, reviewed by an expert panel [E1]. The other substitution at the same residue, p.Arg404Trp, is also Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic [E7]. Residue 404 lies inside the UniProt DNA-binding NBD (392–459) and the InterPro nonamer-binding domain (390–460) [E5]. ScoreCons conservation is 1.0 [E3]. AlphaMissense gives 0.9531 and EVE gives 0.673, both in the pathogenic class [E2, E4]. No experimental structure observes residue 404 [E6]. No retrieved paper measures R404Q activity or binding [E10, G2].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (nucleic acid binding, ranked first): the Arg404 side chain contacts the RSS DNA backbone, and Gln removes that contact [E5, E1]. H2 (stability): the substitution destabilises the NBD fold [E2, E3]. H3 (protein interaction): residue 404 sits in the RAG1 homodimer or RAG2 interface [E8]. Each hypothesis has a refutation criterion in the record [H1, H2, H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
Three candidates were recorded [T1, T2, T3]. T1 is a FoldX stability test. T2 is a P2Rank and ProtVar pocket and interface test. T3, a ligand-contact test, cannot run because no experimental structure covers the residue [T3]. T1 was chosen: it runs now at no compute cost, needs no approval, and bears directly on H2 [T1, plan].

## Result
FoldX predicts a ΔΔG of -0.79 kcal/mol for R404Q at residue pLDDT 93.56, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold. R404W at the same residue gives -0.79 kcal/mol [T1].

## Updated decision
H2 is weakened, since the predicted fold cost is small [T1]. H1 remains favoured, unchanged from the start. The decision did not change [D1]. T1 does not measure DNA contact, so H1 is still untested [T1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
FoldX on a predicted model has errors near 1 kcal/mol, so a neutral value does not show that R404Q is tolerated [T1]. The model confidence is high at the residue, but no experimental structure confirms it. DNA binding, interface contact and recombination activity of R404Q were not measured, so all three hypotheses remain open.

## Next experiment
Run the structural context test T2 to test H3. Then measure whether R404 contacts the RSS backbone in a DNA-bound RAG1 model or structure. A contact under about 4 Å would support H1; no contact would overturn it [NE1]."}
